% Pattern: head/case. A font command of the paper that heads the steps of
% proofs, as \newcommand{\st}[1]{\noindent{\bf #1}} written at the start of a
% line of a proof each time, heads a case of the proof named by its argument,
% whatever the argument says. A font command that is used outside a proof
% too is a font, not a head. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want theorem-1 statement/theorem 1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=theorem-1
% want head-1 other/case -
% want head-2 other/case -
% want head-3 other/case -
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newcommand{\st}[1]{\noindent{\bf  #1}}
\newcommand{\term}[1]{\textbf{#1}}
\begin{document}
\begin{theorem}
The three conditions are equivalent.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
\st{$(a)\Rightarrow(b)$} By the bound.
\st{(ii)} By the choice.

\st{Rough estimates} We bound it.

\term{Small sets} are bounded.
\end{proof}
A \term{small set} is bounded.
\end{document}
